title: [spec-gap][R-02-012] Rendezvous: pinned peer rx_channel is never used for unicast TX in any stack
description: Req R-02-012 (spec/02-physical-link.md 3.3): Rendezvous — Announce includes rx_channel; sender uses the announced channel (TOFU pinning). DIVERGENT (selection layer only, unwired): Announce rx_channel encode/decode/validate exists in all three (python/src/lichen/announce/messages.py:46,97,109; lichen/subsys/lichen/routing/announce.c:144,267,290,304). Python stores _peer_rx_channel (node.py:305, populated :1514-1515) but Node.send (:1558-1604) -> _transmit_peer_schc (:1227-1239) -> link.send() carries no channel; LinkLayer.send (link_layer.py:1284-1294) has no channel parameter and drain loop calls radio.transmit(entry.data) (:1480) dropping the tx_queue entry's channel field (tx_queue.py:198,356,413). Selection helper select_channel(announce_rx_channel=...) exists (link/channel.py:86-116) but has no caller in node/link_layer. C stores entry->rx_channel (gradient.c:243-256) but rg '->rx_channel' finds only the write — no TX read site. Related open beads: fw0f (scheduler accessors use nonexistent state), f0vn (relay stores origin RX under sender), hxqj (range validation). Suggested placement: python link_layer.send + tx_queue channel propagation to radio.transmit; C lichen_link_tx channel selection from gradient entry.
